title: An Ultrahigh-throughput Microfluidic Platform for Single-cell Genome Sequencing
protocol: Prepare the microfluidic mask designs using computer-aided design software.
Have these designs printed with a 10 µm resolution on a circuit board film.
Fabricate the SU-8 master mold as follows for each device.
Prepare a 3-in diameter silicon wafer by pouring approximately 1 mL of SU-8 3025 photoresist onto the center of the wafer.
Secure the wafer on the spin coater chuck by applying suction.
Begin the spin coating with 30 s at 500 rpm, followed by 30 s at the indicated speed.
Remove the SU-8-silicon wafer from the spin coater and soft bake it on a hotplate set to 135 °C for 30 min.
Allow the wafer to cool to room temperature after baking.
Expose the SU-8-silicon wafer with the appropriate microfluidic mask under a collimated 190-mW, 365-nm UV LED for 3 min.
Hard bake the wafer on a hotplate set to 135 °C for 1 min after exposure.
Allow the wafer to cool to room temperature following baking.
Develop the wafer by immersing it into a bath of propylene glycol monomethyl ether acetate (PGMEA) for 30 min.
Rinse the wafer with PGMEA using a squirt bottle.
Rinse the wafer with isopropanol using a squirt bottle.
Place the wafer on a 135 °C hotplate for 1 min to dry.
Prepare PDMS by combining a silicone base with a curing agent in an 11:1 ratio by mass.
Mix the silicone base and curing agent by hand with a stir stick.
Degas the PDMS by placing it into a degassing chamber and applying a vacuum.
Allow the PDMS to degas until air bubbles are no longer visible (typically 30 min).
Pour the degassed PDMS over the master, to a final thickness of approximately 5 mm.
Degas the PDMS again to ensure removal of any air bubbles.
Bake the PDMS and the master at 80 °C for 80 min.
Excise the cured PDMS slab from the baked master using a razor blade.
Punch the inlets and outlets using a 0.75 mm biopsy punch.
Remove any dust and stray PDMS using packaging tape on the feature side of the device.
Clean a 50 mm x 75 mm glass slide by rinsing it with isopropanol and drying it.
Place the PDMS slab and glass slide into the plasma bonder with the features facing up.
Perform the plasma treatment using 1 mbar O2 plasma for 1 min.
Bond the device to the glass slide by bringing the exposed, or face up, sides together.
Bake the device at 80 °C for 40 min following the plasma treatment.
Inject glass surface treatment fluid into one of the inlets to render the microfluidic channels hydrophobic.
Ensure all channels are completely flooded with the solution and repeat the injection for each dropmaker.
Bake the treated device at 80 °C for 10 min to evaporate excess solvent.
Prepare 1 mL of 3% w/v low-melting temperature agarose in 1x Tris-EDTA (TE) buffer.
Keep the agarose solution on a 90 °C heat block until immediately prior to syringe loading.
Prepare the cell suspension.
Resuspend the cells in 1 mL of phosphate-buffered saline (PBS).
Count the cells in a hemocytometer or by flow sorting.
Prepare 1 mL of cell suspension at a final concentration of 2.4 x 10^7 cells/mL for encapsulation.
Spin the cells down at 3,000 x g for 3 min.
Aspirate the supernatant and resuspend the cell pellet in 1 mL of 17% v/v density gradient medium in PBS.
Keep the cell suspension on ice until syringe loading.
Load a 3-mL syringe with fluorinated oil (HFE) containing a 2% w/w perfluoropolyether-polyethylene glycol (PFPE-PEG) surfactant.
Fit the HFE syringe with a 27 G needle and place it into a syringe pump.
Load the cell suspension into a 1-mL syringe, fit it with a 27-gauge needle, and place it into a syringe pump.
Keep the agarose syringe warm with a small space heater set to HIGH, maintaining the temperature at approximately 80 °C near the syringe.
Place the molten agarose into a 1-mL syringe, fit it with a 27-gauge needle, and place it into a syringe pump.
Generate 25 μm microgel drops using the co-flow dropmaking device.
Connect syringe needles to the microfluidic device inlets with PE tubing.
Prime pumps to remove air from the lines before connecting tubes to the device.
Place tubing connected to the outlet into a 15 mL collection tube.
Use flow rates of 800 μL/h for HFE 2% w/w PFPE-PEG, and 200 μL/h each for cell suspension in PBS and 3% w/v agarose during dropmaking.
Place the collection tube at 4 °C for 30 min to ensure complete gelation of the agarose.
Remove the lower layer of oil from the collection tube using a 3 mL syringe fitted with a 20 G needle without disturbing the top layer of agarose droplets.
Add 1 mL of 10% v/v PFO in HFE to the agarose drops.
Pipette the solution up and down for 1 min to thoroughly coat the emulsions.
Spin the conical tube at 2,000 x g for 1 min to collect the agarose microgels.
Remove the PFO/HFE supernatant by aspiration.
Wash the microgels with a surfactant in hexane.
Add 2 mL of 1% v/v sorbitan monooleate nonionic surfactant in hexane to the agarose microgels.
Pipet up and down 10x to mix, ensuring complete breakup of the microgel pellet.
Spin the tube at 1,000 x g for 1 min to collect the microgels.
Aspirate the supernatant to remove the surfactant/hexane solution.
Repeat the surfactant/hexane wash.
Wash the microgels in an aqueous buffer to remove any residual organic solvent.
Add 5 mL of TET buffer to the conical tube.
Pipet up and down 10x to mix.
Spin the conical tube at 2,000 x g for 2 min to collect the microgels.
Aspirate the supernatant to remove the TET buffer.
Repeat the TET wash 2x.
Add 5 mL of 1x TE buffer to the conical tube.
Pipet up and down 10x to mix.
Spin the conical tube at 2,000 x g for 2 min to collect the microgels.
Aspirate the supernatant to remove the TE buffer.
Repeat the TE wash.
Verify the cell encapsulation in the microgels under a microscope at 400X magnification by staining a 10 µL aliquot of gels with 1x nucleic acid stain.

Prepare 1 mL of a lytic enzyme cocktail using 800 µL of TE buffer, 2 µL of yeast lytic enzyme, 30 µL of dithiothreitol, 60 mg of lysozyme, 15 µL of EDTA, 2 µL of mutanolysin, 2 µL of lysostaphin, and 30 µL of NaCl.
Mix the solution by vortexing.
Add the entire 1 mL of the lytic enzyme solution to no more than 1 mL of washed microgels.
Mix by pipetting 10 times.
Incubate the mixture at 37 °C for >2 h in a shaker (the maximum is overnight incubation).
Wash the microgels following lysis via lytic enzymes.
Spin down the microgels at 2,000 x g for 2 min and aspirate the supernatant.
Resuspend microgels in 5 mL of 10 mM Tris-HCl buffer.
Pipette up and down 10 times to mix thoroughly.
Spin the mixture at 2,000 x g for 2 min.
Remove the supernatant by aspiration.
Perform a detergent treatment on the microgels.
Resuspend the gels in a lithium dodecyl sulfate (LiDS) lysis buffer and 60 µL of 0.5 M EDTA to a final volume of 3 mL.
Add 5 µL of Proteinase K enzyme (800 U/mL stock).
Pipette up and down 10 times to mix thoroughly.
Incubate the mixture at 42 °C on a heat block for 1 h.
Spin the conical tube with the microgels down at 2,000 x g for 2 min after incubation.
Remove the supernatant by aspiration.
Wash the microgels with 10 mL of 2% v/v polysorbate 20 in water.
Pipette up and down 10 times to mix thoroughly.
Spin the conical tube down at 2,000 x g for 2 min.
Remove the supernatant by aspiration.
Wash the microgels with 10 mL of 100% ethanol to inactivate any residual enzyme.
Pipette up and down 10 times to mix thoroughly.
Spin the conical tube down at 2,000 x g for 2 min.
Remove the supernatant by aspiration.
Wash the microgels with 10 mL of 0.02% v/v polysorbate 20 in water.
Pipette up and down 10 times to mix thoroughly.
Spin the conical tube down at 2,000 x g for 2 min.
Remove the supernatant by aspiration.
Repeat the polysorbate 20 wash 3 more times.
Pass the solution through a 100-µm cell strainer prior to the last wash.
Resuspend microgels in 5 mL of 10 mM Tris-HCl buffer.
Store resuspended microgels at 4°C for up to 1 week before tagmentation.
Prepare a 500-pM stock of BAR primer in 1x TE buffer.
Dilute the BAR primer stock to a working concentration of 1 pM.
Heat diluted BAR primer to 70°C for 1 minute.

Mix 75 µL high-fidelity hot start master mix, 42 µL PCR-grade water, 3 µL DNA_BAR primer (0.2 µM final), 3 µL P7_BAR primer (0.2 µM final), 6 µL barcode dilution (40 fM final), 6 µL polysorbate 20 (2% final), and 15 µL PEG 6k (5% final).
Mix the PCR reaction components by pipetting up and down ten times.
Draw 200 µL of HFE oil into a syringe and attach it to a needle.
Attach PE tubing to the needle and prime the line by hand.
Insert the end of PE tubing into the target solution and draw all 150 µL of PCR mix into the tubing and syringe.
Load the syringe containing the PCR mix into a syringe pump.
Load a 1 mL syringe with fluorinated oil (HFE) containing 2% w/w PFPE-PEG surfactant, fit it to a needle, and place it in a syringe pump.
Generate 25 µm barcode drops using the co-flow dropmaking device.
Plug the Cells inlet of a co-flow dropmaker device with a small piece of lead solder.
Connect syringes loaded with HFE and PCR mix to the microfluidic device inlets using PE tubing.
Prime the pumps to remove air from the line.
Place the free end of the tubing connected to the outlet into a 0.2 mL PCR tube.
Use flow rates of 600 µL/h for HFE and 200 µL/h for the PCR mix during dropmaking.
Collect drops with approximately 50 µL in each PCR tube.
Remove the lower layer of HFE oil from the emulsions using gel-loading pipet tips.
Replace removed HFE oil with FC-40 fluorinated oil containing a 5% w/w PFPE-PEG surfactant.
Thermal cycle droplets with the following protocol: 98 °C for 3 min, followed by 40 cycles of (98 °C for 10 s, 62 °C for 20 s, 72 °C for 20 s), and a final hold at 12 °C.
Add 1 µL of thermal-cycled barcode emulsion to 10 µL of staining oil.
Incubate them for 5 min at room temperature.
Image droplets by fluorescent microscopy at a 200X magnification using the GFP channel with 497/520 nm excitation/emission wavelengths.
Count the barcode encapsulation rate.
Prepare 500 µL of tagmentation solution using 7 µL of tagmentation enzyme, 250 µL of tagmentation buffer, and 243 µL of PCR-grade water.
Mix the reagents by vortexing and spin down to collect.
Load the tagmentation solution into an HFE oil-backed 1 mL syringe and fit it with a needle.
Spin down the microgel tube for 2 min at 2,000 x g and aspirate the supernatant.
Transfer 200 µL of gels to the top of an HFE-backed syringe using a gel-loading pipet tip.
Seal the nozzle with a small piece of tape.
Spin the microgel syringe for 3 min at 3,000 x g using a 3D-printed centrifuge adapter.
Remove the liquid supernatant from the syringe using a gel-loading pipet tip.
Push the microgel layer to the base of the syringe nozzle.
Fit the syringe with a needle.
Load a 3 mL syringe with fluorinated oil containing a 2% w/w PFPE-PEG surfactant.
Fit the syringe with a needle and place it into a syringe pump.
Connect syringes containing HFE, tagmentation mix, and microgels to the microfluidic device inlets using PE tubing.
Prime the pumps to remove air from the lines before connecting.
Place a piece of tubing connected to the outlet into an empty 1 mL syringe with plunger drawn to the 1 mL line.
Use flow rates of 2,000 µL/h for HFE, 200 µL/h for microgels, and 500 µL/h for tagmentation mix.
Verify the microgel encapsulation rate under a light microscope at 400X magnification.
Fit the syringe containing the tagmentation emulsions with a needle.
Incubate the syringe upright in a heat block or oven for 1 h at 55 °C to fragment genomic DNA.
Replace FC-40 oil fraction with HFE 2% w/w PFPE-PEG to prepare barcode droplets.
Transfer prepared barcode drops into a 1 mL syringe.
Fit the syringe with a needle.
Place the syringe containing barcode drops into a syringe pump.

Prepare 500 µL of PCR mix using specified reagents in order: add 140 µL of PCR-grade water, 10 µL of P5_DNA primer (0.2 µM final), 10 µL of P7_BAR primer (0.2 µM final), 50 µL of PEG 6k (5% final), 50 µL of polysorbate 20 (5% final), 250 µL of Taq Master Mix (2x), 10 µL of isothermal polymerase, and 10 µL of neutralization buffer.
Mix PCR mix by pipetting up and down 10 times.
Spin the mixture to collect it.
Load the prepared PCR mix solution into an HFE-backed 1 mL syringe.
Fit this syringe with a needle.
Place the syringe containing PCR mix into a syringe pump.
Load three 3-mL syringes with fluorinated oil (HFE) containing 2% w/w PFPE-PEG surfactant.
Fit each of these syringes with a needle and place them into syringe pumps.
Load three 1 mL syringes with 2 M NaCl.
Fit each syringe with a needle and set aside.
Merge barcode droplets, tagmented genome droplets, and PCR mix using the double merger device.
Connect the 3 NaCl syringes to the 2 electrode inlets and single moat inlet using pieces of PE tubing.
Apply pressure manually to the syringes until the electrodes are completely filled with salt solution.
Apply manual pressure to the moat syringe until the moat is filled.
Plug the free end of the moat with a small piece of lead solder.
Connect the 3 HFE syringes mounted on pumps to the 2 spacer oil inlets and drop-making oil inlet using pieces of PE tubing.
Prime the pumps to remove air from the line before connecting tubes to the device.
Connect the PCR mix syringe, microgel drops syringe, and barcode drops syringe to their respective inlets using PE tubing.
Shoot all droplet reinjection tubing with an antistatic gun before connecting them to the syringe needles.
Connect a piece of PE tubing to the outlet and place the free end in a 0.2 mL PCR tube.
Connect the needle of the electrode syringe to a cold cathode fluorescent inverter using an alligator clip.
Set the inverter's DC power supply to 2 V.
Run the double merger device with a flow rate of 300 μL/h for tagmented microgel drops.
Set the flow rate at 100 μL/h for barcode drops.
Maintain a flow rate of 1500 μL/h for HFE 2% w/w PFPE-PEG (dropmaking oil).
Run the amplification mix with a flow rate of 600 μL/h.
Set the flow rate at 200 μL/h for HFE 2% w/w PFPE-PEG (barcode spacer oil).
Maintain a flow rate of 700 μL/h for HFE 2% w/w PFPE-PEG (microgel spacer oil).
Collect drops into PCR tubes with approximately 50 μL of emulsion.
Remove the lower layer of HFE oil from the emulsions using gel-loading pipet tips.
Replace the removed HFE oil with FC-40 fluorinated oil containing a 5% w/w PFPE-PEG surfactant.
Thermal cycle at 65 °C for 5 min.
Incubate at 95 °C for 2 min.
Cycle through 30 cycles of 95 °C for 15 s, 60 °C for 1 min, and 72 °C for 1 min.
Thermal cycle at 72 °C for 5 min.
Hold the temperature at 12 °C.
Pool droplets into a microcentrifuge tube.
Break the emulsions using 20 μL of PFO.
Vortex the mixture for 10 s to mix thoroughly.
Spin the tube at 10,000 x g for 1 min to fractionate the mixture.
Remove and transfer the upper aqueous layer from the tube into a new microcentrifuge tube.
Discard the oil phase.
Purify the barcoded PCR product in a spin column according to the manufacturer's protocol.
Elute the purified product in 20 μL of 1x TE buffer.
Proceed to library preparation and sequencing as per subsequent steps.
Prepare the single-cell library for sequencing according to the manufacturer's protocols.
Perform fragment size-selection as per the manufacturer's instructions.
Quantify the prepared library.
Sequence the paired-end library using default chemistry for Read 1 and Read 2.
Use the custom Index 1 primer I7_READ for a 15-bp index read.
Run the script "barcodeCleanup.py" to perform quality control on barcoded reads.
Export single-cell data to an SQLite database.
For control experiments, align reads to known reference genomes using the "-align" flag in "barcodeCleanup.py".
Analyze purity of barcode groups using the script "purity.py".
Confirm high purity values consistent with Figure 6B.
